summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, with a history of chronic pancreatitis, distal pancreatectomy, and intestinal malabsorption. Initial concern was for acute pancreatitis, but lipase levels were normal. Imaging showed no gallstones or obstruction, though significant stool burden was noted. Symptoms were attributed to chronic pancreatitis and malabsorption, exacerbated by inconsistent pancreatic enzyme use and opioid-induced constipation. Pain and nausea were managed with Dilaudid and antiemetics, with improvement on IV fluids and dietary support. Her tachycardia and hypotension resolved with hydration. She was discharged with optimized enzyme therapy, dietary recommendations, and follow-up plans with GI and cardiology.
